claims.title: Settlement by Mande, Kwa, and Mel peoples
claims.summary: Over centuries the region was settled by Niger-Congo-speaking peoples — Mande groups such as the Vai and Kpelle, Kwa groups such as the Kru, Grebo, and Bassa, and Mel groups such as the Gola and Kisi, the last regarded as among the oldest inhabitants.

claims.title: Europeans name the Grain Coast
claims.summary: Portuguese and other European mariners charted the coast and called it the Grain or Pepper Coast after the melegueta pepper traded there; Kru and Grebo seafarers became known along the West African coast.

claims.title: Invention of the Vai script
claims.summary: Momolu Duwalu Bukele and fellow Vai elders are credited with devising the Vai syllabary, one of the few indigenous writing systems created in sub-Saharan Africa, which remains in use; some accounts place its origin earlier.

claims.title: Founding of the American Colonization Society
claims.summary: The American Colonization Society was established in the United States to resettle free-born and freed African Americans in West Africa, drawing together abolitionists and slaveholders with sharply differing motives.

sources.label: History of Liberia: A Time Line

claims.title: Acquisition of Cape Mesurado
claims.summary: Society agents, backed by a U.S. naval officer, secured Cape Mesurado from local rulers as the site for the colony, after an earlier attempt to settle at Sherbro Island had failed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1821-acquisition-of-cape-mesurado, claim TL:LBR:event:1821:acquisition-of-cape-mesurado, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First settlers land and found the colony
claims.summary: Free-born and freed African American settlers went ashore at Cape Mesurado and established the settlement of Christopolis, the nucleus of the colony of Liberia, with the agent Jehudi Ashmun organising its early administration.

sources.label: History of Liberia: A Time Line

claims.title: Christopolis renamed Monrovia
claims.summary: The settlement was renamed Monrovia after U.S. President James Monroe, a patron of the Colonization Society, and the colony was named Liberia, 'land of the free'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1824-christopolis-renamed-monrovia, claim TL:LBR:event:1824:christopolis-renamed-monrovia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Republic of Liberia is proclaimed
claims.summary: Delegates issued the Liberian Declaration of Independence and proclaimed the Republic of Liberia under a U.S.-modelled constitution, making it the first modern republic in Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1847-the-republic-of-liberia-is-proclaimed, claim TL:LBR:event:1847:the-republic-of-liberia-is-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Joseph Jenkins Roberts inaugurated
claims.summary: Joseph Jenkins Roberts, a free man of colour born in Virginia, was inaugurated as the first president of the Republic of Liberia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1848-joseph-jenkins-roberts-inaugurated, claim TL:LBR:event:1848:joseph-jenkins-roberts-inaugurated, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: United States recognises Liberia
claims.summary: Having delayed during the era of slavery, the United States formally recognised the Republic of Liberia in 1862 and concluded a treaty of commerce and navigation with it.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Liberia
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: True Whig Party dominance begins
claims.summary: From 1878 the True Whig Party, the party of the Americo-Liberian elite, held power virtually without interruption for more than a century, marginalising the indigenous majority.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1878-true-whig-party-dominance-begins, claim TL:LBR:event:1878:true-whig-party-dominance-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Firestone rubber concession
claims.summary: The government granted the Firestone Tire and Rubber Company a 99-year concession to lease up to a million acres, creating one of the world's largest rubber plantations and binding Liberia's economy to a single foreign company.

sources.label: The Liberian Civil War (1989–2003) and Firestone

claims.title: William Tubman becomes president
claims.summary: William V. S. Tubman took office as president and would govern until 1971, launching the 'Open Door' policy of foreign investment and the 'National Unification' policy toward the indigenous interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1944-william-tubman-becomes-president, claim TL:LBR:event:1944:william-tubman-becomes-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tolbert succeeds Tubman
claims.summary: On Tubman's death his vice-president William R. Tolbert became president, promising reform but facing mounting discontent over inequality and Americo-Liberian privilege.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1971-tolbert-succeeds-tubman, claim TL:LBR:event:1971:tolbert-succeeds-tubman, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The rice riots
claims.summary: Protests in Monrovia against a proposed increase in the price of rice turned deadly, exposing the fragility of the Tolbert government and the depth of popular grievance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1979-the-rice-riots, claim TL:LBR:event:1979:the-rice-riots, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Samuel Doe's coup ends settler rule
claims.summary: Master Sergeant Samuel K. Doe led soldiers who killed President Tolbert and seized power, ending 133 years of Americo-Liberian and True Whig dominance; thirteen officials were soon publicly executed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1980-samuel-doe-s-coup-ends-settler-rule, claim TL:LBR:event:1980:samuel-doe-s-coup-ends-settler-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Doe confirmed in a flawed election
claims.summary: Samuel Doe was declared the winner of a widely criticised election, formalising his presidency; his increasingly repressive and ethnically partisan rule deepened tensions across Liberia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1985-doe-confirmed-in-a-flawed-election, claim TL:LBR:event:1985:doe-confirmed-in-a-flawed-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Liberian Civil War begins
claims.summary: Charles Taylor's National Patriotic Front of Liberia invaded from Côte d'Ivoire, beginning a brutal civil war marked by ethnic massacres and the widespread use of child soldiers.

claims.title: Samuel Doe captured and killed
claims.summary: President Samuel Doe was captured, tortured, and killed by a rival rebel faction, and a West African ECOMOG force deployed in an attempt to contain the spreading conflict.

claims.title: Charles Taylor elected president
claims.summary: After a 1996 peace accord, Charles Taylor won the 1997 presidential election amid intimidation and war-weariness, ending the first civil war but not the underlying conflict.

sources.label: Liberia — accountability for civil war atrocities

claims.title: Second Liberian Civil War begins
claims.summary: The rebel group LURD launched a new insurgency against Taylor's government from the north, opening a second civil war that would eventually besiege Monrovia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-1999-second-liberian-civil-war-begins, claim TL:LBR:event:1999:second-liberian-civil-war-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Taylor resigns; Accra peace agreement
claims.summary: With rebels besieging Monrovia and an international indictment over Sierra Leone hanging over him, Charles Taylor resigned and went into exile; a comprehensive peace agreement in Accra ended the war and a UN mission, UNMIL, deployed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-2003-taylor-resigns-accra-peace-agreement, claim TL:LBR:event:2003:taylor-resigns-accra-peace-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Taylor convicted of war crimes
claims.summary: The Special Court for Sierra Leone convicted Charles Taylor of aiding and abetting war crimes and crimes against humanity in Sierra Leone and sentenced him to 50 years — the first former head of state convicted by an international tribunal since Nuremberg.

sources.label: Sierra Leone: Landmark Conviction of Liberian Ex-President
Special Court sentences former Liberian leader Charles Taylor to 50 years in prison

claims.title: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf elected
claims.summary: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf won the presidential run-off against George Weah and was inaugurated in January 2006 as the first woman elected to lead an African nation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-2005-ellen-johnson-sirleaf-elected, claim TL:LBR:event:2005:ellen-johnson-sirleaf-elected, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sirleaf shares the Nobel Peace Prize
claims.summary: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, jointly with two other women, for non-violent work on behalf of women's safety and participation in peacebuilding.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-2011-sirleaf-shares-the-nobel-peace-prize, claim TL:LBR:event:2011:sirleaf-shares-the-nobel-peace-prize, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ebola epidemic
claims.summary: Liberia was among the countries worst hit by the West African Ebola epidemic, the largest in history, which killed thousands and overwhelmed a health system already weakened by war before transmission was halted.

sources.label: Ebola Epidemic — Liberia, March–October 2014

claims.title: Peaceful transfer to George Weah
claims.summary: Sirleaf handed power to George Weah, who won the 2017 election — Liberia's first peaceful democratic transfer of power between elected presidents in over seven decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-2018-peaceful-transfer-to-george-weah, claim TL:LBR:event:2018:peaceful-transfer-to-george-weah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Boakai defeats Weah
claims.summary: Joseph Boakai defeated the incumbent George Weah in the 2023 election and took office in 2024, marking another orderly transfer of power in post-war Liberia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Liberia: From the Kru, Grebo, and Vai of the Grain Coast to a settler republic of freed African Americans, the long rule of the Americo-Liberian elite, two devastating civil wars, and Africa's first elected woman president.", terralore.co/country/LBR/chronicle#ev-2023-boakai-defeats-weah, claim TL:LBR:event:2023:boakai-defeats-weah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
